classification.difficultyReason: Reuse a common height across two ladders and subtract their horizontal reaches.

content.prompt:
Two ladders are the same distance up the wall.
The shorter ladder is $4.9\text{m}$ long and makes an angle of $48^\circ$ with the ground.
The longer ladder is $6.7\text{m}$ long.

spec.description: Narrow pale blue rectangular wall on the left; dark blue ground and two ladder segments share the wall's top-right corner. The shorter steeper ladder ends nearer the wall, with 4.9 m on its left. The longer ladder ends farther right, with 6.7 m above/right. A black right-angle square marks the wall-ground junction. The nearer ground angle is labelled 48 degrees. No vertex letters appear.
spec.mathematics: Both right triangles share a height. Hypotenuses are 4.9 m and 6.7 m; the shorter ladder's ground angle is given as 48 degrees. Drawing proportions preserve the visibly not-to-scale source.

inlines.text: How far up the wall do the ladders reach?
Answer correct to one decimal place.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the angle, to the nearest degree, that the longer ladder makes with the ground?

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the distance between the ladders on the ground. Answer to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ and $y$ be the horizontal reaches of the shorter and longer ladders.
$$\begin{align*}x&=4.9\cos48^\circ\\y&=\sqrt{6.7^2-(4.9\sin48^\circ)^2}\\d&=y-x\\d&=\sqrt{6.7^2-(4.9\sin48^\circ)^2}-4.9\cos48^\circ\\d&\approx2.3\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
